answer.generated: Concurrency control and locks are closely related in managing transactions within a database system. Concurrency control mechanisms ensure that multiple transactions can execute concurrently without violating data integrity. Locks play a crucial role in this process by controlling access to shared resources. When a transaction attempts to modify a database object, it may acquire a lock to ensure exclusive access, preventing other conflicting transactions from modifying the same object simultaneously. This lock-based approach helps maintain consistency and prevent issues such as deadlocks, thereby supporting efficient and reliable transaction processing.
